subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the Children of Echoes

150130802.text: Nechca must have woken up and wants to get out of bed on her own... Sorry, I'll go check on her first.

150130803.text: Nechca! Don't try to get out of bed, just tell Mom if you need anything!

150130804.text: You go ahead and take care of Nechca, Auntie.

150130805.text: #Let's go, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. There are a few things I want to tell you.

150130101.text: Xilonen! Good thing you're here, I'm wondering if I can—

150130102.text: The shelf on the left, second row down, first axe on the right... that one's yours. The garden hoe belongs to Iknal and the hammer is Pacal's, so make sure you take the one that's yours.

150130103.text: I haven't even said why I'm here... But looks like you're about to head out for a break?

150130104.text: Yes, but I'm going to take it right here. The temperature's just perfect today.

150130105.text: Really? But doesn't it feel a lot hotter than usual? I really don't want to stay out in this heat.

150130106.text: Exactly. In hot weather like this, customers don't tend to stick around and talk when they're coming to place orders or pick up the goods.

150130107.text: I see... Oh, here comes another customer. I'll just leave you to it then, and pick up my axe.

150130110.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we meet again. You two seem to be in good spirits.

150130111.text: How's your Pilgrim's Chronicle been? Run into any issues?

150130113.text: Good. It was also my first time receiving a Pilgrim's Chronicle. Even though I've already turned it over to you...

150130114.text: There are still a lot of things that could go wrong, so I wasn't sure if there would be any issues.

150130115.text: Huh? So, uh... what are the chances that something might still go wrong?

150130116.text: Less than the chances of Mualani accidentally falling off a Spiritway, I'd say.

150130117.text: Oh, well that definitely would never happen...

150130118.text: I've found the axe, Xilonen. Thanks a lot.

150130119.text: By the way, Nechca's birthday is coming up real soon. Are you planning to visit her?

150130120.text: I've prepared a gift, and was just getting ready to take it to her.

150130121.text: *sigh* You're not planning on giving the kid a full set of pliers again, are you? Or lemme guess, woodworking tools?

150130123.text: That's right. Flowers will wither, toys will break, and snacks are quickly forgotten once they're eaten...

150130124.text: But a set of durable work tools will always stay with you, and get you through many sticky situations.

150130128.text: Still, I won't be giving Nechca any tools this year. She wrote me a letter saying that she'd like a copy of "Tequil the Brave."

150130129.text: The book is not what you'd call a bestseller, but luckily, I have a few copies in my collection. They were really old editions that were published a long time ago, but they should still be readable...

150130130.text: Haha, children her age love fairy tales. The last time I was at Tlazolli's, I even brought Nechca a—

150130131.text: Huh? Wait... what did I bring her again? It must have been her favorite thing, but... Uh... Why can't I remember it anymore?

150130132.text: It is quite hot today, seems you're about to pass out from the heat. Do you even remember your own name?

150130133.text: My memory can't be this bad. It's just these last few days... *sigh* I've been forgetting things for some odd reason.

150130134.text: In that case, why don't you use the Blazegem Inscription you have as a memo to engrave some important things to remember?

150130135.text: After all, that Inscription will never wear out, and it's easy to carry... I'd say that's quite a fitting use for it.

150130136.text: Ahem... You do have a point, but... my Inscription is almost already full.

150130126.text: I make these myself, and it's a lot of work. But if you'd like a set, I can make some time and forge one for you.

150130127.text: Great! We often camp out in the wild, but a set of Xilonen's tools would make pitching a tent and starting a bonfire a whole lot easier.

150131101.text: You explain your encounter with Tlazolli to Xilonen...

150131102.text: So that's how you met her... She even wants to use Volcanic Crystal as a forging material... Guess she's really pulling out all the stops for her daughter.

150131105.text: Then let's just go and ask. Come on, I want to give her the book anyway.

150131106.text: Huh? Wait a second, aren't birthday gifts supposed to be a surprise?

150131107.text: If we ask Nechca, then she'll know what gift we'll be getting her, and that would ruin the surprise!

150131108.text: But if you don't ask her, then how will you know what kind of present she would like?

150131109.text: Here's another idea. Perhaps you can also give her a storybook based on what she wrote in her letter. That might be a good option.

150131110.text: Easy enough, I have loads of those in my bag.

150131111.text: But shouldn't we give it a little more thought? If we all give her books, it might seem like we didn't put much effort into it.

150131112.text: Xilonen, have you really never asked her what she would like the most? There must be something else she'd like besides books.

150131113.text: Unfortunately, no. Nechca's illness has kept flaring up over the past few years. Apparently, she couldn't do anything during that time other than rest in her bed. She didn't even have the strength to talk to anyone.

150131114.text: It wasn't until recently that she started to recover from her illness and regained the strength to write letters to others.

150131115.text: Anyway, there's no need to overthink it. Worst case scenario, I can split the book into two volumes and we can each give her one.

150130201.text: Go on now, Iengu. Nechca is still resting.

150130204.text: Oh? What a surprise! And even Xilonen is here, too...

150130206.text: It's been a while since I've seen you last, Auntie.

150130207.text: I received Nechca's letter. She wanted a copy of Tequil the Brave, right? I've brought the book for her.

150130208.text: There are several editions of the book in Natlan, and I wasn't sure which version she'd prefer.

150130209.text: I asked a messenger from the Scions of the Canopy. It seems this softcover edition is one of the most popular options, so I bought it for Nechca.

150130210.text: Heh, you haven't changed a bit, Xilonen.

150130211.text: Let's go inside. I was just boiling some Xocoatl, so you can all try some.

150130212.text: Xilonen used to love drinking Xocoatl. When she was little, she would always have several cups every time she came to visit me.

150130213.text: You were already a big girl by the time I finally had my Nechca. Alright, for now, let's—

150130216.text: #{NICKNAME}, please help me get her into the house.

150130219.text: Be good, Iengu, and don't get in the way!

150130221.text: Alright, let's get indoors. Watch your step now, Auntie.

subQuests.subQuestName: Help Tlazolli into the room to rest

150130301.text: Sorry, Nechca's illness has been flaring up recently, so I was up for a few nights.

150130302.text: I suddenly started to feel dizzy in the sun... I hope I didn't scare you.

150130303.text: Have a seat. I'll fetch you a few cups of Xocoatl. Please wait a moment...

150130304.text: I've already brought them over. This cup's for you, Aunt Tlazolli. And these are for you two.

150130305.text: #Xocoatl... What does it taste like? Paimon's heard that it can be pretty bitter... {NICKNAME}, could you give it a try first?

150130306.text: Don't worry, Auntie always adds lots of sugar. It won't be bitter.

150130307.text: The last time you came to visit, you were still just a kid. But now you're a pillar of the Children of Echoes... No, of all Natlan even!

150130308.text: It's all thanks to the drinks I had here, and the books I happened to read.

150130309.text: You've been close for quite some time, then?

150130310.text: We heard that you two are from the same tribe... but Paimon had no idea you were so close.

150130311.text: When I was little, my parents were always talking about how skilled Auntie was at forging Ancient Names, and how she was such a good role model for all the rest of us...

150130312.text: The moment I became idle at home, they would toss me into Auntie's workshop to watch and learn...

150130313.text: Then your parents would go back, I would boil you a pot of Xocoatl, and let you play in the house.

150130314.text: Yeah. Then I would drink, and listen to you banging away with your tools in the workshop.

150130315.text: But eventually, she moved out of the tribe to find some more space for her workshop, and I didn't have the chance to visit again after that.

150130316.text: But why did you seem so familiar with the place when you went to the kitchen for the drinks just now?

150130317.text: Because the layout of this place is identical to her old house.

150130318.text: Let me see... Ah, that should be Nechca's bedroom, then?

150130319.text: That's right. Hehe, I remember you used to hunker down in the room to read and draw...

150130320.text: But you're all grown up now... Even if you wanted to live here, I'm afraid you've already outgrown Nechca's bed.

150130323.text: That's how Nechca sees Xilonen, too. Whenever she's feeling better, she always asks me when her penpal sister would be coming to visit.

150130324.text: Well, I'm here now, and even brought a gift as an apology. I'll leave the book here.

150130325.text: You said Nechca asked you for the book? I hope it wasn't too much trouble to get... Really, I'm surprised that she even asked you for a present. When she's at home, she'd even ask me for permission to eat some snacks.

150130326.text: *sigh* Maybe I've been too strict with her. She's obviously starting to like her big sister more than her own mother!

150130327.text: Really? Well, I'd say I really haven't done enough to deserve the title of big sister.

150130328.text: I wasn't able to help her when she was sick, and I didn't even come and properly visit her that many times. The only thing I've been able to do is to help her find some books.

150130329.text: Don't be too hard on yourself, Xilonen. You have great responsibilities as the Name Engraver of the tribe. We both know you are far too busy to take care of her.

150130330.text: The responsibilities on your shoulders also became far heavier when I... gave up on my work.

150130331.text: You just had more important things to tend to, Auntie... No one in the tribe blames you. We all know that Nechca needs her mother's care.

150130332.text: But that doesn't change the fact that I gave up on my work. And... even now, I still have not found the courage to pick up my hammer again.

150130333.text: I'm sorry to leave you to shoulder all the responsibilities alone, Xilonen.

150130335.text: Whoa, why so somber all of a sudden... Uh, don't be so sad, everyone! Hasn't Nechca gotten better lately?

150130336.text: Relax, Auntie. I can handle the work. But once Nechca is back on her feet, you should get back to work and let me have a vacation.

150130337.text: You'll be the one who's busy then, and I'll be sitting at the side drinking Xocoatl and cheering you on.

150130338.text: Heh, if that day really comes, you can have as much Xocoatl as you like.

150130401.text: Hmm, no one's come to deliver the ingredients yet... Paimon thought we'd see someone come flying down on a Yumkasaur as soon as we came out.

150130402.text: A messenger from the Scions of the Canopy wouldn't be flying here. They usually come climbing down the cliffs nearby.

150130403.text: No need to look, there isn't anyone on the cliffs.

150130407.text: Hey, you there! Sorry, but does Tlazolli live around here?

150130408.text: Oh, are you the one who's supposed to deliver the ingredients?

150130410.text: Ingredients? Are you kidding? I was nearly eaten myself!

150130411.text: Ugh, never mind that now. Those monsters are still hot on my heels! Please, you've gotta help me!

150130412.text: Xilonen, we... Huh? Where'd she go?

150130413.text: Whoa! She's already gone up to fight the monsters! Let's go help her out!

150130501.text: Seriously! Since when have there been so many monsters here?

150130601.text: Alright... That should be it for the monsters. Was easier than I thought.

150130602.text: It also seems we're in luck — the goods weren't damaged either.

150130603.text: Strange... we didn't see any monsters on the way here.

150130606.text: Yeah right! I use this road to deliver goods all the time, and I've never been attacked like this before.

150130607.text: It's the main road in and out of the tribe, so people often come here to clear out any monsters. This area's usually very safe.

150130608.text: I don't know what happened, but it seems like all the monsters around here have gone berserk. Even the docile Tepetlisaurs are in a frenzy!

150130609.text: *sigh* Tlazolli doesn't even forge Ancient Names anymore, so why can't she just move back to the tribe?

150130610.text: If she comes back, Nechca will even be able to find some playmates. She's so young, and hasn't even—

150130611.text: Uh... Nechca's playmates... No, wait. I feel like my kids have played with her before. They've even told me about Nechca's favorite game... If I remember right, it was...

150130612.text: Strange, I always remembered it before... How could I forget all of a sudden...?

150130613.text: Look at that! He has a Blazegem Inscription, too.

150130701.text: Ah, you're finally back. What took you so long? I was starting to worry.

150130702.text: We ran into some small problems, but everything's fine now.

150130703.text: Alright, as long as everything's okay now. You all have a seat, I'll get the food ready. It won't take long.

150130704.text: Tlazolli gets to work on the food. After cooking for some time, delicious dishes are set on the table one after another...

150130705.text: Whoa, there's so much tasty food! You're amazing, Tlazolli!

150130706.text: They were all pretty simple dishes to make. Don't be shy. Dig in, everyone!

150130708.text: Hehe, Paimon will help herself! Hmm, Paimon will have some of this, and this... oh, and this!

150130711.text: Can I get another serving, please?

150130712.text: Y—You're done already!? Do you even chew when you're eating!?

150130713.text: Of course. Didn't I say that I chew up the fish bones?

150130714.text: I'll have just one more fish, and leave the rest for Nechca.

150130715.text: It's okay, just go ahead and eat all you'd like. Nechca can't eat these dishes anyway.

150130716.text: Her body is too weak to digest these kinds of things. I'll just make some broth for her.

150130717.text: Oh no... But, Paimon thought she had already recovered from her illness.

150130718.text: Injuries caused by the Abyss cannot be undone. The doctor said the fact that she's stable is already quite a miracle.

150130719.text: But it's okay! Nechca can talk to me now, and can even hold my hand... That's more than I could ask for.

150130720.text: ...Even if she will never again know that I am her mother.

150130722.text: The doctor said the Abyss has had an irreversible effect on Nechca's soul. She... She's lost all her memories from before she was injured.

150130723.text: The doctor also said that this sort of memory loss isn't like simply forgetting something. Rather, she can no longer remember anything from before that fateful day.

150130724.text: Huh? But, how does that happen?

150130725.text: You know about the woven scrolls that the Masters of the Night-Wind use to record things, right?

150130726.text: Well, generally speaking, forgetting things is like when the woven scrolls would gradually start to fade. As long as you re-paint and weave the threads again, the faded memories will come back to life.

150130727.text: But the case of Nechca's memory loss is as if her woven scroll had been cut in two, and the portion from the past was burned to ashes.

150130728.text: The books she loved to read, the flowers she took joy to grow... and the time she spent in this house were all cut off by the Abyss, and can never be retrieved again.

150130729.text: As one example of that, Nechca now only sees me as... a strange, unfamiliar Auntie who claims to be her mother.

150130730.text: She's a good kid, and doesn't want to upset this lady who's been taking care of her so much, so she still calls me "Mom."

150130731.text: But I've always had a feeling that she's constantly wondering about things like... Where is her real mother? Why is she stuck here in this house? Was she abandoned?

150130732.text: Nechca really has no idea that her real mother is right in front of her, and has never left...

150130733.text: So, you plan on recreating Nechca's woven scroll all by yourself?

150130735.text: Or should I say, you've already started reweaving that scroll long ago?

150130710.text: But Paimon can't reach that dish... Could you give Paimon some? C'mon, c'mon!

150131301.text: That kid... She's just like Nechca.

150131701.text: Hello again! Back for more tea? I can put on another pot.

150131703.text: Oh? You'd like to know about their... technical details?

150131704.text: As you're friends of Xilonen, I'm willing to share that information with you, yes... Let me pick something simple to start with.

150131705.text: They... Are actually accidental byproducts from my first time forging an Ancient Name.

150131706.text: Then, I accidentally made a mistake with the Phlogiston Engraving of an Ancient Name, creating some kind of "deviation" in the functionality of the Ancient Name.

150131707.text: It could not guide the "memories" and "emotions" that people feel, but rather it could take certain "memories" within itself.

150131708.text: At first, I thought it was utterly useless, so I tossed it in with the other defective products. But after Nechca fell ill, I suddenly thought of this "defective" Ancient Name... which is now known as a "Blazegem Inscription."

150131709.text: ...Nechca lost her memories of the "past." But that past was clearly real... and there are many witnesses to those events.

150131710.text: I can use that Blazegem Inscription to extract memories related to Nechca from the witnesses.

150131711.text: And then, by gathering all those memories together, create an entire "memory bank" about Nechca's past for her.

150131712.text: That way... My little Nechca can come home. She'll remember... that Mama will always be by her side.

150131714.text: I do apologize for making you worry, but... It's just as I said. I could collapse at any moment.

150131715.text: In order to forge "Ancient Names," I have paid a high price... Or perhaps I should say, I have given everything I can give, even my little Nechca.

150131716.text: I'm not bitter towards anyone, nor do I expect anything in return... Right now, all I want is to help Nechca get better.

150131717.text: And for that, I will offer everything I have and am.

150131719.text: Goodbye. The roads outside are tough going, so please be careful.

150136001.text: Xilonen! Good thing you're here, I'm wondering if I can—

150136002.text: The shelf on the left, second row down, first axe on the right... that one's yours. The garden hoe belongs to Iknal and the hammer is Pacal's, so make sure you take the one that's yours.

150136003.text: I haven't even said why I'm here... But looks like you're about to head out for a break?

150136004.text: Yes, but I'm going to take it right here. The temperature's just perfect today.

150136005.text: Really? But doesn't it feel a lot hotter than usual? I really don't want to stay out in this heat.

150136006.text: Exactly. In hot weather like this, customers don't tend to stick around and talk when they're coming to place orders or pick up the goods.

150136007.text: I see... Oh, here comes another customer. I'll just leave you to it then, and pick up my ax.

150136010.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we meet again. You two seem to be in good spirits.

150136011.text: How's your Ancient Name been? Run into any issues?

150136013.text: Good. It was my first time working with the Lord of the Night to forge an Ancient Name, and you're not even from Natlan.

150136014.text: There are still a lot of things that could go wrong, so I wasn't sure if there would be any issues.

150136015.text: Huh? So, uh... what are the chances that something might still go wrong?

150136016.text: Well, less than the chances of Mualani accidentally falling off a Spiritway, I'd say.

150136017.text: Oh, well that definitely would never happen...

150136018.text: I've found the ax, Xilonen. Thanks a lot.

150136019.text: By the way, Nechca's birthday is coming up real soon. Are you planning to visit her?

150136020.text: I've prepared a gift, and was just getting ready to take it to her.

150136021.text: *sigh* You're not planning on giving the kid a full set of pliers again, are you? Or lemme guess, woodworking tools?

150136023.text: That's right. Flowers will wither, toys will break, and snacks are quickly forgotten once they're eaten...

150136024.text: But a set of durable work tools will always stay with you, and get you through many sticky situations.

150136028.text: Still, I won't be giving Nechca any tools this year. She wrote me a letter saying that she'd like a copy of "Tequil the Brave."

150136029.text: The book is not what you'd call a bestseller, but luckily, I have a few copies in my collection. They were really old editions that were published a long time ago, but they should still be readable...

150136030.text: Haha, children her age love fairy tales. The last time I was at Tlazolli's, I even brought Nechca a—

150136031.text: Huh? Wait... what did I bring her again? It must have been her favorite thing, but... Uh... Why can't I remember it anymore?

150136032.text: It is quite hot today, seems you're about to pass out from the heat. Do you even remember your own name?

150136033.text: My memory can't be this bad. It's just these last few days... *sigh* I've been forgetting things for some odd reason.

150136034.text: In that case, why don't you use the Blazegem Inscription you have as a memo to engrave some important things to remember?

150136035.text: After all, that Inscription will never wear out, and it's easy to carry... I'd say that's quite a fitting use for it.

150136036.text: Ahem... You do have a point, but... my Inscription is almost already full.

150136026.text: I make these myself, and it's a lot of work. But if you'd like a set, I can make some time and forge one for you.

150136027.text: Great! Hehe, we often camp out in the wild, but a set of Xilonen's tools would make pitching a tent and making a bonfire a whole lot easier.
